subject: AWS Private Offer: activation staging, buyer approvals & seller-assist checklist
messages:
From: Claire Moss <claire.moss@zencloud.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Matthew Hayes <matthew.hayes@zencloud.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private offer questions — term split and approvals

Hi Rachel,

Thanks for the quick demo yesterday — the team is excited. Before we lock the private offer, procurement asked for a clear activation plan so they can align Finance and Legal. Two specific asks:

1) A short buyer-facing activation checklist (who signs, timeline for activation after signature).
2) Evidence pack for SOC2 + data residency for our EU customers (we only need a pointer to the artifacts).

We'd like to move quickly but can't commit longer than 12 months without a buyer approval queue mapped out. Can your team put together a seller-assist checklist that covers pre-activation entitlements and expected activation lag?

Appreciate it — CCing Matthew who will coordinate procurement.

Best,
Claire
ZenCloud — Head of Cloud Procurement

Attachments: none

From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
To: Claire Moss <claire.moss@zencloud.com>, Matthew Hayes <matthew.hayes@zencloud.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Aug 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private offer questions — term split and approvals

Hi Claire / Matthew —

Thanks — we can absolutely do that. Quick notes and next steps from our side:

- Seller-assist activation checklist (we will draft): who signs (buyer legal / buyer finance), expected timeline (signature -> activation window), required evidence items, and recommended canary activation for the first billing cycle.
- For SOC2 + residency: we'll provide a single ZIP with SOC2 Type II summary, SOC2 attestation pointer (hosted S3 link), and a short note on our EU region controls.
- Term/length: we recommend a 12-month initial PO with an automatic renewal opt-out rather than a 24-month lock; this addresses buyer hesitation while keeping activation simple. If Finance insists on multi-year pricing we can map an approval lane for CFO signoff (see staging options below).

Proposed staging for activation (short):
1) Contract execution + DocuSign (0–2 business days)
2) Seller sends evidence pack + activation checklist to buyer (same day as signed)
3) Redwood ops schedules activation (1–2 business days)
4) Soft activation / canary project with reduced quota (3–5 business days)
5) Full activation and billing (within 7 business days)

I'll attach a draft activation checklist and PO template for your procurement to preview. Ben will own legal entitlements; Karthik will own billing/activation windows.

Rachel
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference

Attachments: po-draft-v2.pdf (preview), activation-checklist-draft.docx

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Claire Moss <claire.moss@zencloud.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Aug 2027 09:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private offer questions — term split and approvals

Claire — thanks for the ask. A few legal/contract points to flag so procurement isn't surprised:

- PO term length drives approval routing in AWS Marketplace (12 months -> buyer procurement only; >12 months may require CFO signoff and Marketplace private offer gating).
- Escrow / billing proration: we'll propose a pro-rated first invoice for activation month to smooth CFO concerns.
- Audit evidence: we'll include a permissions map and the SOC2 attestation link in the evidence ZIP; we generally avoid shipping full reports, but we can coordinate an NDA if ZenCloud needs full artifacts.

Action items for us:
- I'll update the PO draft with the pro-rata billing clause and an "activation acceptance" item that buyer signs to mark the canary as successful.
- Karthik to confirm activation SLA (target 7 business days) and whether we can compress to 3 for enterprise pilots.

Ben
Sr. Contracts Manager — Redwood Inference

Attachments: updated-po-clauses.txt

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Claire Moss <claire.moss@zencloud.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Aug 2027 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private offer questions — term split and approvals

Claire / team —

We're good to support the 12-month PO with the activation staging Rachel proposed. Operational notes and seller-assist items below:

- Activation SLA: standard 7 business days; for pilots we can target 3 business days if ZenCloud confirms a single signing authority and provides the required evidence immediately after signing.
- Billing: we'll do a pro-rated first invoice and disable automatic renew until ZenCloud confirms production readiness.
- Approvals mapping: if ZenCloud keeps PO <=12 months, no CFO signoff in AWS Marketplace is required. If they extend to >12 months, please expect an approval queue that can add 3–5 business days depending on buyer controls.
- Evidence pack: we've uploaded the packet to a secure link and included a short README. Claire, please confirm if you want full SOC2 artifacts (requires NDA) or the summary + attestation pointer is sufficient.

Soojin (CS Ops) — I'll need your help scheduling the canary activation once Claire confirms the signing path.

Karthik
Head of Revenue Ops — Redwood Inference

Attachments: zencloud-evidence-pack.zip
